description: OriDB v3.0 trial release: the Confirmed origin tier only, carried forward from OriDB v2 with explicit evidence records.
inclusion_rule: An origin is Confirmed if its interval overlaps at least one plasmid (ARS) assay positive or one 2D gel electrophoresis record.

sacCer3.note: Lifted from sacCer1 with the UCSC chain file. Each record keeps its original sacCer1 position in source_chromosome/source_start/source_end and the outcome of a base-for-base sequence check in lift_status.

provenance.source: nieduszy_oridb MySQL dump (OriDB v2.1.0 cerevisiae / v1.0.0 pombe)

known_issues.text: Non-Confirmed v2 origins that overlap direct evidence and need curator review: sc_ori 79 (Dubious), sc_ori 84 (Dubious), sc_ori 741 (Likely). They are Likely or Dubious in v2, so they are not in this release and cannot be linked here.

OriDB intervals and the ARS features SGD and UCSC show for sacCer3 should describe the same object - the assayed fragment - and mostly they differ in a way that looks like a coordinate error rather than biology. Of the 410 Confirmed cerevisiae origins, 293 overlap a replication-origin feature in UCSC's sgdOther table for sacCer3. 258 of those pairs share an IDENTICAL end coordinate and differ only at the start: 244 by exactly 2 bp and 14 by 1 bp, with the SGD feature always starting inside the OriDB interval. For 194 of the 2 bp cases the OriDB start is the position of a PCR primer located in the genome by its own sequence, so the SGD feature begins two bases inside the primer that defined the fragment. This has not been confirmed with SGD and should be raised with them before either set is treated as authoritative at base resolution. Separately, 117 Confirmed origins have no SGD origin feature and 81 SGD origin features overlap no Confirmed origin.

51 lifted cerevisiae intervals do not have identical sequence in sacCer3 - substitutions, or an indel that changes interval length. lift.note: Systematic names are NOT recomputed. They are coordinate-derived labels from the v2 build and are cited as such in the literature, so they stay fixed; a name like X-212 therefore need not match the lifted midpoint.
